citations.claim: pre-impact controlled body slow under force limit, touching intruder
first violating step: post-collision velocity jump causes controller force to exceed fmax

counterfactual.change: moved intruder body 1 start x from 1.3 to 18.5 so no high-speed collision with controlled body occurs; velocity stays small and force stays under fmax

explanation: At step 28 bodies 0 and 1 are touching (gap 0.005) with controller force only 6.56. The fast intruder collides and impulsively kicks controlled body 0 from speed ~2.9 to ~10.27 at step 29. The waypoint velocity-error law kp*velocity-error then demands ~486.9 N, far above fmax 72.67, because the commanded force is computed from post-impact velocity error without clamping to fmax. Moving the intruder away (counterfactual) removes the impact and the spike.
vision_note: A small red ball drops onto the larger controller-driven ball near the green waypoint, closing the gap through steps 26-27 until they touch at step 28. At step 29 the larger ball is knocked sideways while the red ball rebounds, showing the impulsive impact that causes the controller force spike.
